text: Amazon SDE new grad behavioral round focused on Ownership and Dive Deep. Interviewer asked: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical approach. Expect STAR answers with metrics. Follow-ups probed customer impact and what you would do differently.

Amazon OA/phone screen: two coding problems. Common themes include arrays, hash maps, and string manipulation. Candidates should discuss time/space complexity and edge cases. Interviewer often asks to optimize a brute-force solution.

Amazon internship loop: deep dive into a resume project. Questions on architecture choices, bottlenecks, monitoring, and failure modes. Strong candidates quantify scale (users, latency, data size) and connect decisions to Deliver Results.

Goldman Sachs engineering analyst interview mixes coding with structured thinking. Expect clarity under pressure, explanation of assumptions, and sometimes markets/probability intuition. Weak communication is heavily penalized even with correct answers.
GS behavioral: Why Goldman? Describe a high-pressure deadline. How do you prioritize when stakeholders conflict? Interviewers look for composure, precision, and ownership of outcomes.

Cognizant ACE technical interview emphasizes CS fundamentals: OOP pillars, DBMS normalization, OS process vs thread, and a clear walkthrough of one academic project. Communication and basics matter more than advanced system design.

Cognizant ACE HR/communication round: introduce yourself, explain a project simply, discuss strengths/weaknesses, and willingness to learn. Candidates who ramble or cannot explain their own resume projects struggle.

Google SWE interviews are heavy on algorithms: graphs, DP, trees. Interviewers care about problem decomposition, testing strategy, and complexity analysis. Talking through edge cases aloud is expected.
Microsoft SWE loop balances coding with collaboration and product sense. Expect questions about conflicting priorities, inclusive teamwork, and designing a simple feature end-to-end.
Amazon LP interview: Customer Obsession and Bias for Action stories. Use STAR. Quantify impact. Be ready for 'What would you do differently?' and 'How did customers benefit?'
